findings.title: Failed USE on new connection permanently breaks pool refilling
findings.claim: current_keyspace is set before USE is verified to succeed, so a keyspace typo or a later-dropped keyspace causes every new connection to be discarded with ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace and refill retried with growing backoff forever, leaving the pool permanently Broken(UseKeyspaceError) once existing connections die.

findings.title: Shard-aware extra connection drop path omits dec_total_connections
findings.claim: The branch handling an extra shard-aware connection (else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()) drops the connection without calling dec_total_connections, even though it was counted on open, so total_connections leaks upward permanently for connections landing on the wrong shard (e.g. behind NAT).

findings.title: Stale failed USE for outdated keyspace discards connection instead of retrying
findings.claim: If current_keyspace changes while an older USE is still in flight and that USE fails, the connection is dropped and marked as error rather than resent through start_setting_keyspace_for_connection with the new keyspace, unlike the success branch which already re-checks evt.keyspace_name against current_keyspace.

findings.title: New ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant misrepresents CQL errors as connection-fatal
findings.claim: Adding ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError with #[from] makes UseKeyspaceError convert into ConnectionError via ?, so callers see a pool-level Broken error for what is really a CQL error (e.g. RequestError(DbError::Invalid) for a missing keyspace), even though ConnectionError is documented as meaning the connection can no longer be used and should be dropped, risking misclassification by callers.
